title: The Stokes, Whipped Cream and Java
summary: Whipped Cream was written for the Stokes as a joke; he had Al Hirt in mind after Java.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And you were with a group called the Stokes and it was then that you put out, you wrote Whipped Cream, which was later covered by Herb Albert. Right. Right.

Right. Whipped Cream was written for the Stokes as a joke. We'd do things in the Stokes, even though it was supposed to be a conventional rock band. We would do things like Spike Jonze and we'd rehearse the tune sometime that we had to tear a piece of paper or drop a piece of tin on the floor. So we had lots of things that was in the order of Whipped Cream. Whipped Cream was one of them.
You had written Java a couple of years before, about five years before that, for yourself, hadn't you? And then that was picked up by All Herb.

Right. Right. Right. Actually, in the writing of Whipped Cream, one thing that did make Whipped Cream a bit unique from the other tunes right in that same year of instrumentals, I did have Al Hurt in mind after he had did Java. I hadn't thought of Java for a trumpet or anything. And Al Hurt did inspire a lot of songs. It's easier to write what Al Hurt in mind. You can write forever. It's like writing for Aaron Neville's Iron Man Thomas. You can write for them without stopping.
